basis: The 2025-26 annual report (PDF page 5) says the gallery, operating as The Art Gallery at Harbourfront, is governed by its Board of Directors and is a registered Canadian charitable organization.
The about page says the gallery is managed by a volunteer Board of Directors, the board page lists the directors, and the CanadaHelps page shows it as a CRA registered charity.
The staff and board page says the gallery is incorporated as a non-profit society under the Societies Act of British Columbia, is a registered federal charity and is governed by a Board of Directors.
The about page says Western Front is a non-profit artist-run centre that incorporated as a non-profit society in 1974.

The about page says grunt is run by staff, contractors and volunteer board members, and the CanadaHelps page lists the registered charity Unit 306: Society for the Democratization of the Arts under the grunt gallery name.

Note 1 of the March 2025 financial statements (PDF page 8) says the Society is incorporated under the Societies Act of British Columbia and is a charitable organization registered under the Income Tax Act, and the board page describes the Board's oversight of the CEO.
The governance statement says the Museum is incorporated under the Canada Not-for-profit Corporations Act from 4 October 2012, is a registered charity and is led by a Board of Trustees.
The board member information package says Plug In ICA operates as a not-for-profit exhibition space (PDF page 3) and lists approval of the annual budget among board duties (PDF page 8).
The staff and board page lists a Board of Directors with a President, and the CanadaHelps page shows Urban Shaman Inc. as a CRA registered charity.

The Winnipeg Art Gallery Incorporation Act (sections 1 and 5) continues the gallery as a corporation of members run by a board of governors, and the Manitoba government listing (PDF page 1, which names the Act as its authority) says the Board appoints the Director, approves annual program and financial plans, and includes one City of Winnipeg appointee and up to three provincial appointees.
